title: ABA Problem in Lock-Free Reclamation
pattern: Performing a Compare-And-Swap (CAS) on a raw shared pointer where nodes are freed or recycled back to an allocator immediately after a successful exchange.
why_bad: If Thread 1 reads pointer `A`, then gets suspended, and other threads pop `A`, free it, push a new node `B`, and then reuse the memory of `A` to push a new node, the pointer address becomes `A` again. When Thread 1 resumes, CAS succeeds because the address matches, but the linked target `next_node` points to outdated memory, causing silent heap corruption [21:22].
detection: Performing raw pointer CAS operations in concurrent structures without incorporating epoch-based reclamation (EBR), hazard pointers, or garbage collection abstractions [21:22].
counterexample: Use standard libraries such as `crossbeam-epoch` which defer reclamation until no thread holds references to the epoch [21:23].
fix: Incorporate Epoch-Based Reclamation (EBR) or hazard pointers to ensure nodes cannot be recycled until all active readers have completed their traversals [21:23].
source: *Locking & Deferred Processing* (LKMM), Chapter 9: seqlocks vs RCU [21:22].
